title: std::cin and handling invalid input
recap: Formatted extraction reports failure through the stream state. While failbit is set, later extractions will keep failing; clear the state before ignoring a bad line. Ignoring up to newline prevents the same bad token from being retried forever.

EOF is not ordinary invalid text: if the source has ended there is nothing left to retry. A final successful extraction may set eofbit without failing, so handle successful extraction before treating EOF as failure.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.

warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.

Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement readQuantity() using std::cin. Read an integer at the beginning of each attempted line; discard the rest of that line. Return the first integer in [1,20]. On invalid text, an out-of-range number, or integer overflow, discard that line and retry. On end-of-input before a valid value, return -1. A line beginning "3 extra" is accepted as 3; this is intentionally not a strict whole-line parser. Do not print prompts. Test scaffolding supplies simulated input automatically.
hints: Use an extraction as the condition of an if statement.
After failure, check eof(), then clear() and ignore through newline.
After successful extraction, discard the rest of the line before accepting or retrying.
